title: Commissioners in earlier listings who are officers of City-paid organizations
question: Do the 2019-2024 listings of boards and commissions, and three current member pages, name members who are officers of organizations the City pays, beyond those the site’s “Who sits on boards and commissions” page found in 2025-2026?
finding: The 2019 listing yields 484 seat lines (83 vacant) on 61 bodies and 381 holder names. The 2020 listing yields 613 seat lines (129 vacant) on 89 bodies and 451 holder names. The 2022 listing yields 795 seat lines (118 vacant) on 76 bodies and 517 holder names. The 2024 listing yields 745 seat lines (110 vacant) on 68 bodies and 438 holder names. 3 holders are confirmed by their own Form 700 as connected to a City-paid organization on whose return they appear; 2 of them are not in the site’s “Who sits on boards and commissions” page, and for 0 the body oversees a department that paid the organization $25,000 or more since fiscal 2019. 203 name-only matches are counted and not named.
how: Each older listing is read as laid-out text: a seat is a line starting with a seat number under a "Seat Holder" or "Current Seat Holder" heading, and the holder is the text in that column. The 2019 and 2020 listings print only vacant and expiring seats. Matching then follows the “rosters” analysis exactly (first and last name, one organization in the tax-return file, confirmation by the member's Form 700).
limits: The 2019 and 2020 listings show only seats that were vacant or expiring, so they miss most sitting members. Name match, confirmed by a second record. Many seats are reserved for people from funded or regulated organizations, and holding one is permitted; the question is recusal from decisions about the organization.
